questions.question: Should total fleet shrink with multi-trip or remain fixed while actual used vehicles decline?
questions.answer: For the causal single-trip versus multi-trip comparison, hold the same defensible availability ceiling and let actual used physical vehicles decline endogenously. Do not shrink the ceiling by an unsupported factor. If a separate long-term fleet-planning study is desired, derive a strategic fleet from multi-trip demand realizations and then hold it fixed in daily operations.

basis.evidence: Available set K is fixed; z_k/N_veh determines actual use. Higher per-vehicle fixed cost reduces used vehicles while trips can remain unchanged.
Strategic fleet is the 95th percentile of vehicle requirements over 50 multi-trip VRP demand simulations, then K is fixed for daily routing.
Trips are packed into physical vehicles; y selects actual vehicles and Table 3 reports the resulting used fleet.
V can be exogenous or algorithm-determined, but benchmark comparisons fix V within a subproblem; no proportional shrink rule is proposed.

questions.rejected_interpretation: The literature does not support treating ceil(0.25*R_d) or the observed 33.4% used-vehicle reduction as a new ex-ante availability coefficient.

questions.question: Does this paper need a maximum number of trips per vehicle per day?
questions.answer: No numerical cap is supported unless an external operational, labor, or regulatory rule supplies one. Let the working horizon, driver/vehicle hours, customer time windows, charging, depot turnaround, and non-overlap constraints bound realized trips. If a finite trip index set is required computationally, use a provably safe bound rather than presenting it as an operational assumption.

basis.evidence: Allows any number of trips per day; legal driver schedules and maximum driving time bind.
No count cap; sum of route durations on one vehicle must be within T_H.
No count cap; depot hours, customer windows, and consecutive-trip scheduling bind.
R is only a sufficiently large trip-index integer; realized trips are bounded by [E,L], capacity, distance and timing.
One or more trips per route; T and turnaround Delta bind.
Main instances use 3 or 5; appendix illustration uses 2. No operational basis is supplied, and max-trip tests had no clear differences.

questions.question: If fixed cost remains billed per trip, what multi-trip benefit can be reported without overclaiming?
questions.answer: Report the reduction in actual physical vehicles/fleet requirement, trips per used vehicle or trip-to-vehicle ratio, and any separately observed distance, time, energy, emissions, or service-coverage changes. Do not report fixed-cost or total-cost savings caused by vehicle reuse when the number of billed trips is unchanged.

basis.evidence: The motivation links multi-trip to fleet fixed cost, but equation (1) charges F^k for every active trip u; physical-vehicle reuse cannot reduce that term.
Per-physical-vehicle billing P*z_k makes N_veh a legitimate cost channel and reports N_veh separately from N_trip.
A_v is per physical vehicle across periods, B_v is per vehicle-period route, and actual used vehicles are reported.
With no vehicle fixed cost, the paper reports travel-time outcomes rather than claiming fleet fixed-cost savings.
With no fixed-cost term, results are total travel time, feasibility, and algorithm quality.

questions.project_safe_wording: For the same 1040 delivery trips, multi-trip scheduling uses 693 physical vehicles instead of 1040, reducing the physical fleet requirement by 347 vehicles (33.4%). Because the current fixed cost is billed per trip, this reuse does not reduce fixed cost.
questions.prohibited_wording_under_current_account: Multi-trip reduces fixed cost or total cost by 33.4%.

one_sentence_literature_conclusion: In true physical-vehicle multi-trip papers, benefits are most often expressed as lower physical fleet requirement or higher utilization and, only when fixed cost is billed per physical vehicle, as lower fleet cost; algorithm benchmarks often report travel time and feasibility instead.
